newsitem.title: UK: China to humiliate Britain at HK handover - paper.
newsitem.headline: China to humiliate Britain at HK handover - paper.

text.p: China plans to humiliate Britain at the ceremony marking the transfer of power over Hong Kong by using the occasion to swear in the colony's future unelected provisional legislature, the Sunday Times reported.
Beijing has invited scores of high-profile guests to the June 30 ceremony, when Hong Kong will be formally handed back to China under the terms of a 1984 Sino-British agreement.
Although the ceremony is just weeks away the two sides are still far apart on how the colony should be run in future.

Britain is especially angry about Beijing's decision to dissolve the colony's locally-elected council and replace it with the provisional legislature, whose candidates have been chosen by the Chinese.

The Sunday Times, quoting unidentified British officials and Hong Kong sources for its report, said Britain felt the Chinese clearly intended to exploit the handover to imply international support for the decision to impose the new unelected council.
The newspaper said British Prime Minister Tony Blair was considering whether to boycott the handover ceremony. A government spokeswoman said Blair had not yet made up his mind whether to attend.

Hong Kong pro-democracy activists say China will clamp down on the colony after it takes control. Britain and the United States have made clear to Beijing that they will keep a close eye on the situation.
